data.one_liner: Reactive primitive and state management solution based on signals and node coloring.
data.what_it_does: State_beacon provides reactive primitives like signals, derived values, effects, and asynchronous state handlers. It automatically tracks dependencies and updates dependent widgets or calculations when values change.
use_when: You want signal-based reactivity for Dart and Flutter apps without code generation.
You need to handle complex asynchronous state transitions with automatic loading, error, and data states.
You want fine-grained widget rebuilding using .watch(context).
avoid_when: You prefer strict BLoC architectural patterns and event-driven architectures.
Your project standardizes entirely around Riverpod or Provider.
strengths: Fine-grained reactivity without boilerplate or code generation.
Built-in support for asynchronous operations via FutureBeacon and StreamBeacon with AsyncValue states.
Extensive helper methods for debouncing, throttling, buffering, filtering, and undo/redo.
weaknesses: Relatively new package with a smaller ecosystem compared to Riverpod or Provider.
Accidentally accessing dependencies after an async gap will fail to track them.
data.setup_notes: No special native permissions or build_runner steps required.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a compile-safe, provider-based dependency injection and state management solution.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you require strict separation of concerns using events and states with predictable state transitions.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a simple, classic inherited widget wrapper for dependency injection and basic state changes.
